blocks.text: Traits controlled by alleles on the sex chromosomes are sex-linked traits, and the phenomenon is sex linkage. Sex-linked traits are really X-linked, because the Y chromosome usually carries almost no functional genes; that is why the ratios of sex-linked traits differ in males and females.
The alleles of a very few traits are found on both X and Y. Such traits are equally distributed among males and females and are called X-Y-linked or pseudo-autosomal traits.
